# All Set

A Mac desktop that looks the way you want: a **Dynamic Island** on the notch, **desktop widgets**, whole-desktop **themes** and **live wallpapers**, in one app. Native (Swift 6, AppKit + SwiftUI), Apple Silicon, macOS 14.2 or later.

What's in it, in numbers (generated from the code; CI fails if they drift):

- 54 widget kinds
- 91 widgets in the gallery
- 1310 widgets from themes
- 131 themes (whole desktops)
- 36 built-in live wallpapers
- 15 design themes

The full inventory is in `CONTENT.md`.

## What it does
- **Dynamic Island.** Hover or click the notch: Now Playing with artwork and controls, live system readings, Notes with alarms and a stopwatch. While closed, live activities appear beside the notch (music, volume, charging, low battery, output changes). Macs without a notch get a virtual one in the menu bar.
- **Desktop widgets.** Clocks, calendar, weather, photos, system stats, notes, focus timers, GitHub, football and music widgets and more, each in several sizes and card styles. They snap to a grid; Arrange mode moves and resizes them; every word in a widget can be renamed. Each display keeps its own widget size, and a new monitor or resolution refits them.
- **Themes.** Complete desktops (widgets, their look and a wallpaper) applied in one click, previewed first if you like, and undone with Undo or Restore Previous Desktop (which survives a relaunch). Football and music themes are built on moods; every player, club and fixture in them is invented.
- **Wallpaper.** Built-in live wallpapers drawn on your Mac (no download), your own looping videos, or a library folder of your own. It pauses when covered, locked, asleep, in Low Power Mode or on battery, and sets a matching still as the system wallpaper; your own comes back when you turn it off.

## Core and Extras
All Set is those four things. Everything else is an **Extra**, switched on and off in Extras › Manage: Window Snapping, Workspaces, Clipboard History, Shelf, Sound Mixer, TapTap (knocks), AI Screenshot and System Monitor. An extra that is off starts no controller, keeps no timer, holds no keyboard shortcut and asks for no permission, and its page leaves the navigation. A new install starts with every extra off; an install from before extras existed (2026-10-17) keeps them all on.

The window has four places, **Island**, **Desktop**, **Extras** and **Settings** (⌘1–⌘4), with each place's pages beneath; ⌘K searches every page.

## Privacy
Everything you make is files in one folder on your Mac (`~/Library/Application Support/AllSet`); Settings › General backs it up and restores it. There is no account, analytics or tracking, and crash reports stay on your Mac unless you export them. Some widgets and features fetch what they show (weather from Open-Meteo, photo search from Openverse, featured photos from Picsum, GitHub data; your screenshot goes to Anthropic or OpenAI only when you send it with your own key, and you're asked first). **Settings › General › Network use** lists every connection the app can make, when, and what it sends; a test keeps that list complete.

Permissions are asked for only when you switch on something that needs one: Accessibility (Window Snapping, Workspaces, some TapTap actions), Calendars (calendar widgets), Audio Recording (Sound Mixer). Settings › General › Permissions shows where each stands.

## Install
Download `AllSet-<version>.dmg` from the repository's Releases, open it and drag All Set to Applications.

A release signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple opens normally. Until the project has a Developer ID (see `Documentation/OWNER_ACTIONS.md`), releases are signed ad hoc and macOS blocks the first open:
- **macOS 15 and later:** open All Set once (it's blocked), then System Settings › Privacy & Security › Security › **Open Anyway** next to All Set, and confirm with your password.
- **macOS 14:** right-click All Set in Applications › Open › Open.

Ad-hoc builds also lose Accessibility and other permissions on every update, because macOS ties them to the signature; a Developer ID build keeps them.

## Updates
About › Check for Updates… and the menu bar panel use Sparkle 2 with EdDSA-signed updates from the repository's Releases. Builds made before the project's update key exists have updates switched off entirely (no checks, no network).

## Restoring macOS and uninstalling
- **Settings › General › Restore macOS settings All Set changed** gives macOS back its ⌘⇧5 screenshot shortcut (if you let All Set take it) and turns the live wallpaper off, which puts your own system wallpaper back. Safe to run anytime.
- **Settings › General › Uninstall All Set…** does that, removes the login item, optionally moves your data to the Trash, then moves the app to the Trash.
- Already deleted the app while it was running? Run `scripts/uninstall.sh` (add `--data` to move the data folder to the Trash too). It only moves things to the Trash, never deletes.

## Requirements
- **A Mac with Apple Silicon** (M1 or later). Intel Macs aren't supported: the app is built for arm64 only, and its sensor features (temperatures, the motion sensor) exist only on Apple Silicon.
- **macOS 14.2 or later.** Developed on macOS 26; CI builds for exactly macOS 14.2 so nothing newer slips in unguarded. It has not yet been run on a real macOS 14 or 15 Mac (see `Documentation/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`).

To build it: Xcode (for the Swift 6 toolchain and SDK). Building, testing, the debug tools and releasing are in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## How the tricky parts work
- **Now Playing.** macOS 15.4 and later only give Now Playing info to Apple-signed processes. `MediaController` starts `/usr/bin/perl`, which is Apple-signed, with a short loader script that loads `libAllSetMediaHelper.dylib`; it reads MediaRemote and sends JSON lines back. The helper must answer within 3 seconds and is retried at most 3 times a launch; then Now Playing says it's unavailable.
- **Private interfaces.** Now Playing, temperatures (IOKit HID), the motion sensor, Carbon hot keys, Core Audio taps, macOS's symbolic hot keys and TCC's preflight are all behind `Capabilities`: each has a kill switch (`defaults write com.pratik.allset capability.<name>.disabled -bool YES`) and a status in Settings › General › Compatibility. A macOS update that breaks one stops only the feature built on it.
- **The notch window** is a borderless, non-activating panel just above the menu bar that accepts clicks only over its shape.

Because of these, All Set can't be sandboxed and won't pass Mac App Store review. It's distributed directly, signed with a Developer ID and notarized.
